local_modal_close.summary: Close the current local modal after a successful selection or operation.
local_modal_close.authoring: Apply the selected record to page state first, await any required read, then closeModal. Closing a modal does not select a record or run a tool by itself.
local_modal_close.security: Navigation only; grants no tool, persistence, or publication authority.

state_observation.summary: Observe an already running operation with a read-only state probe while its page is mounted.

entry.action: <ordinary declared read-only skill action with resultStateKey>

binding.lifecycle: Runs immediately, then at intervals >=1000 ms, skips overlapping calls of the same id, and stops on page/modal destruction. once=true runs on mount only and still requires a positive intervalMs.
binding.location: Declare autoActions on the actual page schema or modal route schema. This is not a widget input.
binding.followups: Use normal followup updateState/refresh actions to select a newly completed result and refresh its data. A terminal status disables the observer through enabledIf.

state_observation.authoring: Use only to read run state/progress. Keep effect execution in a Core-owned durable continuation. Restore the selected active run on reload using a read, then resume observation; never start a new paid operation from autoActions.
state_observation.security: This observer grants no permission and must not submit, approve, poll-and-advance, or retry paid work. Requests use normal caller and runtime admission.

browser_history.summary: Project semantic page state into Back/Forward-safe, non-secret query values.
browser_history.authoring: Use push for user-visible semantic destinations such as a section or selected record; use replace for transient filters; use ephemeral for state that must never enter browser history. Bind only scalar state. Back/Forward reprojects state and never replays callSkill, workflow, approval, publication, pairing, or other effects.
browser_history.security: Secret and runtime-topology query keys are rejected. Intent and one-use codes are not page state and must not be bound. Declared application parameters are included in copied links and cleared at scenario boundaries.

application_entity_address.summary: Restore an application-owned selected entity without rendering another entity's seed first.
application_entity_address.authoring: Core owns topology, not application entity semantics. The application publishes a lightweight selection independently of heavy inspection and maps the visible entity title as well as its id. Defaults, source and explicit URL are applied in one PageState emission. required waits for the entity source before mounting widgets; identityKeys keeps metadata with its entity. Explicit links, user selections and Back/Forward retain address authority over late source echoes. Without an explicit selection, genuine source changes update the URL. Declare readPriority=interactive for a user-opened picker; its bounded read lane does not wait behind background page reads.
application_entity_address.security: An address is not authorization or a business command. Back/Forward only restores local selection state and cannot replay paid generation, publication or approval.

deprecated_interfaces.replacement: action.type:navigateModal for a local declared modal; action.type:navigate for a public view
deprecated_interfaces.migration: For an exact local id under ui.application.modals, use navigateModal with params.modalId. For a public cross-application view, declare it under ui.application.interfaces.<owner>.views, bind the implementation through implements and schema.interface.routes, then use navigate with params.to and params.modalId.
deprecated_interfaces.compatibility: The runtime may read legacy openModal actions, but Builder and generators must not emit them.

layouts.title: Document flow
layouts.summary: A readable ordered surface for content and lightweight actions.

responsive.compact: ordered stack

postconditions: Content order and reading focus remain stable across viewports.

layouts.title: Collection
layouts.summary: Search, filters, commands and one list, table, cards, tree or similar collection.

responsive.compact: collection with disclosed filters and adaptive actions

postconditions: Exactly one collection region owns the primary browse task.

layouts.title: Collection and detail
layouts.summary: A selectable collection with contextual details or an inspector.

manifest.variant_composition: For one page with state-selected sections, preserve the base layout and append a complete layout.variants entry with id, when, pattern, density, contentWidth, scroll, regions and interaction. A variant replaces the active region set; include every shared toolbar/navigation region plus collection and detail regions in that variant. Do not append section-only regions to the base layout.regions.

responsive.compact: collection plus declared sheet, drawer or route

postconditions: Row activation is explicit and detail remains reachable on compact viewports.

layouts.title: Master detail
layouts.summary: Hierarchical navigation or a master surface leading to one focused detail task.

responsive.compact: drawer or route to focused content

postconditions: Navigation and current detail have separate focus identities.

layouts.title: Dashboard
layouts.summary: A responsive overview of independent metrics and status regions.

manifest.composition: Declare shell-wide controls in a toolbar or navigation region; both span the dashboard width. Declare independent peer dashboard blocks as separate layout.regions with role=status or role=utility and place each widget in its owning area. role=main spans the dashboard width. Multiple widgets in one region remain one vertical region; a single region cannot produce a peer dashboard grid.

responsive.compact: ordered single-column overview

postconditions: Peer regions retain a stable semantic order when wrapping.

layouts.title: Board workbench
layouts.summary: A board-centered task surface with tools and optional context.

responsive.compact: bounded horizontal board with disclosed context

postconditions: Layout regions do not duplicate the board widget's lane semantics.

layouts.title: Task flow
layouts.summary: A form, wizard or bounded workflow with persistent commands and status.

responsive.compact: single task path with reachable commands

postconditions: The primary completion command remains reachable and unambiguous.

layouts.title: Settings
layouts.summary: Grouped preferences with optional navigation and explicit apply semantics.

responsive.compact: route or drawer navigation with focused group

postconditions: Preference scope and save behavior are visible.

layouts.title: Workbench
layouts.summary: A dense multi-region surface for repeated professional work.

manifest.panel_contract: Shared workspace panels use the same renderer in desktop and schema modals. Region size.minPx/preferredPx/maxPx/grow are honored. size.resizable=true enables pointer and keyboard resizing; size.remember=true persists only presentation width, isolated by subnet/surface/page/variant/region. Arrow keys resize, Shift accelerates, Home/double-click reset, Escape cancels a drag. Compact presentation is chosen from actual container width and declared minima; drawer/sheet/route/overflow regions use accessible local disclosure. Declare widget.sizing=fill to consume remaining panel height. No application-specific names or CSS are required.

responsive.compact: declared drawer, sheet, route and overflow disclosure

postconditions: Each region has explicit ownership, scroll and compact presentation.

components.title: Composable group
components.summary: Compose existing widgets into a row, stack, adaptive grid, section or disclosure with header/body/footer slots.

manifest.children: Declare children as ordinary widget configurations, at most 100 per group and 8 levels deep. Each child has its own unique id, normal datasource/actions/visibleIf, area=content, optional slot=header|body|footer and sizing=content|fill. No executable HTML or CSS.
manifest.layout: inputs.layout=row|stack|grid|section|disclosure; gap=none|xs|sm|md|lg. A grid uses columns=1..12 or responsive minItemWidthPx. expandedStateKey is local presentation state only.
manifest.lifecycle: Collapsed disclosure bodies are unmounted; normal scoped widget drafts survive in browser memory. Closing or opening never commits a form or starts a job.

responsive.compact: Rows wrap and adaptive grids collapse within the available container

postconditions: Child actions retain their normal owner and authorization.
A fill-sized widget consumes available space without a fixed viewport height.

components.title: Task progress
components.summary: Display authoritative asynchronous job stages, measured progress, elapsed time, reason for stopping and cancellation.

manifest.data: Bind a read-only datasource returning a TaskProgress record; inputs.taskKey optionally selects its path. Status, stages and progress come from the provider. Progress is optional; do not fabricate a timed percentage.
manifest.cancel: Declare on=cancel; event carries run_id and revision. The button appears only when provider can_cancel=true and the task is active. A successful command requests cancellation; only an authoritative terminal state confirms completion. The renderer never continues jobs, approves permissions or starts paid calls.
manifest.ownership: Server owns durable execution. Reload and remount only read. Keep selected historical artifact separate from active task.

responsive.desktop: Bounded task card with stages and cancellation
responsive.compact: Wrapping status, timing and controls

postconditions: Changing task identity cannot apply an old cancellation response to a new task.
All subscriptions and elapsed timers stop on disposal.

components.title: Image comparison and manual masks
components.summary: Original on the left and result on the right with shared native-pixel zoom and pan, displayed scale, fit/100%, result-only mode, download, optional vector edit/protection masks and a service-defined protected context frame.

manifest.annotations: Optional pair.annotations follows image.annotations.v1.schema.json. Up to16 independent layers declare side=original|result, stable id/label/role, visible/editable, optional native-resolution raster mask with encoding=alpha|luminance, plus ordered add/subtract vector corrections. All layers retain oriented native coordinates; no mask downscaling. Every raster base must have exactly the paired image dimensions. The pair is always rendered in one original coordinate system. Do not combine contours from another result.
manifest.annotation_editor: editorStateKey adds annotationDraft:{generation,version,layerId,document}. Local layer/erase/undo/redo commands never call AI. The annotation draft is isolated by scope, source and exact result asset and survives remount in browser memory. External layer-changing commands must target that annotation generation/version. annotationSave emits annotations, context mask/crop, sourceId, generation, version and optimistic revision; the service validates ownership and rasterizes the immutable base plus ordered deltas. A unified submit must snapshot both legacy mask/crop and annotationDraft transactionally. Raster bases are immutable; Clear removes the selected editable layer coverage only.

annotation_commands.envelope: Write one fresh object to editorCommandStateKey: {sourceId:$state.editor.sourceId,generation:$state.editor.generation,action:<name>,value?:<payload>}. editor is the configured editorStateKey. Use canEdit for tools and ready for submit; loading or active painting blocks external commands.
annotation_commands.guard: For undo, redo, clear, layerVisibility, addLayer and addAnnotationStrokes additionally send annotationGeneration:$state.editor.annotationDraft.generation and annotationVersion:$state.editor.annotationDraft.version. These are distinct from legacy mask generation/version. A saved acknowledgement also needs exact legacy generation/version and the new optimistic revision.
annotation_commands.layer: action=layer, value=<existing layer id string>. Selection only; no inference or persistence.
annotation_commands.layerVisibility: action=layerVisibility, value={id:<existing layer id>,visible:<boolean>} plus annotation guards.
annotation_commands.tool: action=tool, value=pan|crop|edit|erase when annotations exist. edit adds coverage to the selected editable layer; erase subtracts. Protection is an independent layer selected through action=layer, not the legacy protect tool. Without annotations tools are pan/crop/edit/protect according to permission mode.
annotation_commands.addLayer: action=addLayer, value=<complete valid annotation layer with strokes array and no raster mask> plus annotation guards. New layer becomes active.
annotation_commands.addAnnotationStrokes: action=addAnnotationStrokes, value=[{kind:add|subtract,radius:<positive native pixels>,points:[{x,y}]}] plus annotation guards. Appends to the active editable layer; preserve all existing layers and bases.
annotation_commands.history: action=undo|redo|clear plus annotation guards. Undo/redo restore whole gestures including crop and layer geometry. clear removes coverage only from the active editable layer.
annotation_commands.fitBounds: action=fitBounds, value={x,y,width,height} wholly inside the native frame. View change only.
annotation_commands.permissionMode: action=permissionMode,value=elements|rectangle changes legacy edit permission and preserves strokes. Crop tool creates, moves and resizes the context rectangle independently of selected annotation layer.

manifest.crop_editor: The crop tool creates, moves and resizes an existing rectangle with native-pixel edge/corner handles. Undo/redo preserves complete operations, including crop and layer corrections. Pointer cancellation rolls back the unfinished gesture.

inputs.pairKey: Optional path inside the dataSource payload to the pair record.
inputs.originalKey: Pair record path to original media descriptor or URL; defaults to original.
inputs.resultKey: Pair record path to result media descriptor or URL; defaults to result.
inputs.original: Optional explicit original media descriptor, resource reference or image URL.
inputs.result: Optional explicit result media descriptor, resource reference or image URL.
inputs.editableMasks: Boolean; show crop, edit/protect brushes and Save masks. No inference or saving on painting/zooming.
inputs.maskToolbar: Boolean, default true. Set false to move editing controls into an authored sidebar; this hides only the built-in mask toolbar, not the canvas or comparison controls.
inputs.showMaskSaveButton: Boolean, default true. Set false when an owning unified processing action persists the exact draft before submitting; hiding the button does not save or infer.
inputs.sourceIdKey: Pair-record path for the original owner identity used by the editor bridge; defaults to id. Use a stable identity such as photo_id when pair.id changes with result versions.
inputs.sourceRevisionKey: Pair-record path for the original optimistic revision; defaults to revision. A dirty draft retains the revision on which it was drawn until that exact draft is acknowledged as saved.
inputs.editorStateKey: Optional PageState output key. Publishes {sourceId,revision,generation,version,canEdit,ready,dirty,editing,mask,tool,radius,permissionMode,canUndo,masksVisible}. canEdit means the original is loaded and editable, including when a rectangle is incomplete or too small. Use canEdit (plus matching sourceId) for crop, brush, mode, undo and clear controls; do not gate those tools on ready, because an incomplete rectangle needs the crop tool to become valid. canEdit is false during loading, image errors, painting or disposal. ready additionally requires a valid complete mask and must gate submission. mask is a detached complete adaos.image_masks.v1 value, including crop and protection. ready is false during source loading, a pointer stroke, invalid geometry or disposal. A unified start action must require ready and matching sourceId, and send mask plus revision with current form values to one owning transactional command; persistence failure must stop submission. Painting never performs a tool call. With this bridge, browser-memory drafts are isolated by stable sourceId/original and survive renderer disposal, photo switching and result updates; a changed server mask does not silently replace dirty edits. A browser reload does not persist an unsubmitted draft.
inputs.editorCommandStateKey: Optional PageState input key for sidebar commands: set a fresh object {sourceId,action,value?,generation?,version?,revision?}. sourceId must match the loaded original. generation identifies the original draft, survives same-original media/result refreshes and renderer disposal, and changes for another master/scope. Tool commands require loaded geometry and are ignored while loading/editing. saved acknowledgements and mode intents wait for the same original to finish refreshing; a later manual view choice supersedes a queued mode. Actions: tool (pan|crop|edit|protect, respecting permission mode), permissionMode (elements|rectangle), radius (finite number1..500), undo, clear, toggleMasks, mode (original|compare|result), fit, zoom (positive number), saved. A saved acknowledgement must contain the exact generation/version sent and the new optimistic revision; it cannot clear a later edit. addStrokes accepts value {strokes,crop?} and requires exact generation and version of the reviewed draft. Only valid edit strokes are appended (total max500); red protection, existing strokes and an existing crop are retained. crop can initialize an absent crop only. Applying switches to elements mode, displays masks and marks the local draft dirty, without saving or submitting. Stale, replayed, invalid and foreign-source suggestions are rejected. An application must show proposal reasons and ask the user to apply, gate application on matching photo/generation/version, and label the explicit switch to element masks. Commands only manipulate the local editor and never submit or save on their own.
inputs.brushRadiusStateKey: Optional numeric PageState key for an immediate sidebar range/number field; the viewer mirrors the active brush radius to this key and accepts finite local updates, clamped to 1..500 pixels. No persistence or inference is triggered.
inputs.labels: Optional localized labels: compare, original, result, fit, download, difference, changedPixels, changedArea, differenceLegend, differenceMismatch, differenceLoadError, masks, permissionMode, elementsMode, rectangleMode, rectangleHelp, contextFrame, contextFrameHelp, pan, crop, edit, protect, radius, undo, clear, saveMasks, unsaved, empty, maskHelp, loadError, mismatch.
inputs.downloadFilename: Optional download filename override; otherwise inferred from pair.download or result descriptor/URL and its MIME.
inputs.noticeKey: Optional pair-record path for a plain-text notice shown prominently above the image controls with role=status. Use for diagnostic or rejected candidates, for example noticeKey=resultLabel. Only strings are rendered, through escaped text interpolation; an absent or empty value clears the notice, including updates of the same media pair. Does not change image loading, editing, downloads or submission.

manifest.actions: on:maskSave provides $event.mask. Bind to a declared scoped resource command or skill tool. A successful action clears the dirty indicator.

data_shape.download: Optional separate image descriptor/URL for the selected export. Original/result can remain canonical lossless PNG masters while this resolves a final JPEG export. Defaults to result; filename comes from this descriptor, never from the PNG master when downloading JPEG.
data_shape.difference: Optional exact difference metadata: {mask:<owned image descriptor/URL>,width,height,changed_pixels,total_pixels,comparison_basis:lossless-rgb}. The owning skill compares native decoded RGB channels of the same oriented/color-managed lossless base and PNG master; one differing channel makes the pixel changed. The mask shades unchanged pixels with semitransparent alpha and leaves changed pixels transparent. Counts are integers, total_pixels=width*height, max50MP. The viewer verifies actual mask geometry before enabling the toggle, displays native changed count/area, uses the shared transform on both panes, and resets the toggle on pair change. No CSS difference blend or browser approximation is used. JPEG is a separate final download, never the comparison basis.
data_shape.masks: Optional masks:{schema:adaos.image_masks.v1,width,height,permission_mode?:elements|rectangle,context_border_px?:integer1..256,crop?:{x,y,width,height},strokes:[{kind:edit|protect,radius,points:[{x,y}]}]}. Coordinates, radius and context_border_px are pixels of the EXIF-oriented original; max 500 strokes, 512 points per stroke. Missing permission_mode means elements: edit strokes grant permission and crop provides context. Explicit rectangle mode requires a crop and grants permission inside it, ignoring edit strokes while retaining them for switching back. When the owning service supplies context_border_px, the crop must leave a positive interior after subtracting this width on all four sides. The viewer shows a yellow protected ring of REAL crop pixels, shows green rectangle permission only inside the ring, clips green edit strokes to that interior, preserves the frame on explicit save/reload and renders it with the shared native-pixel transform at any zoom. A border may be supplied before a crop exists; drawing a crop then shows its ring. Missing context_border_px preserves legacy display. Red protection retains priority in both modes. The owning skill must validate its authoritative policy and implement the same perimeter and red protection in provider mask and final CPU composite; browser metadata cannot weaken server protection. A changed context_border_px refreshes the pair even when media URLs stay the same. The viewer does not run AI, segment background or rasterize masks.

responsive.desktop: Two equal simultaneous panes with one shared transform.
responsive.compact: Two simultaneous panes remain side by side; original/result-only modes and zoom buttons allow detailed work.

limitations: Original and result must have identical native dimensions; mismatched results are withheld from comparison.

Legacy permission masks are manual vector strokes, not automatic segmentation. For a workflow declaring those permissions, the owning skill must validate and rasterize them and composite only within the edit mask minus protection. Independent annotation roles do not imply a composition policy.

Without the opt-in editorStateKey bridge, pair identity changes retain legacy pair-scoped drafts. With the bridge, choose sourceIdKey for a stable original identity, validate sourceId/revision/geometry on the server and atomically persist the submitted draft before any provider call. Browser-memory draft retention is not durable server storage.
postconditions: Original is left and result right in comparison mode.
Zoom percentage represents CSS pixels per original pixel; both panes share zoom and pan.
Zoom, pan, mode changes and painting make no AI requests.
Mask save is explicit and dispatched through the declared AdaOS action.

components.title: Resource board
components.summary: A field-driven board projection of one flat resource collection into ordered lanes.

data_shape.lane_membership: Each item laneKey value equals one declared lanes[].id.

item.optional_projection: cardFields maps arbitrary typed resource fields without domain-specific card code

responsive.desktop: all lanes are equal peer columns when width permits
responsive.compact: lane order is preserved in a horizontally scrollable rail

interactions.query: Prefer dataSource.kind=resourceQuery for typed filters, search, sort, cursor, and relevance over Resource Workbench.
interactions.crud: Use action.type=resourceOperation for ordinary create/update/delete. action.target is resource_type; params.operation_id selects the declared operation.
interactions.button_scope: inputs.buttons are repeated on every card. Do not put a board-level Add command there; use the lane add event.
interactions.drag_drop: Set inputs.dragDrop=true and declare on=move. The event spreads displayed item fields at top level, including id and revision when supplied by the read, then adds fromLaneId, toLaneId, previousIndex, currentIndex, interaction, laneKey and patch. The lane value is already optimistic. For owned tools bind callSkill params.id=$event.id, revision=$event.revision and patch=$event.patch; not event.record.revision. The renderer awaits the action and rolls back on false/denied result or throw. Do not fetch a newer revision to overwrite a stale view. resourceOperation(update) remains supported for ordinary declarative mutations.
interactions.accessible_move: A lane selector is rendered with draggable cards so the same move is available without a dragging gesture.
interactions.lane_create: Declare on=add to expose one add command per lane. The event provides laneId and defaults containing the lane field, but never payload. When required fields must be entered, on=add opens a typed create form; it must not directly create from $event.payload.

limitations: The renderer never becomes data authority; Resource Workbench or a declared domain command applies mutations.
dragDrop=true requires an on=move persistence action; the renderer only provides optimistic feedback and rollback.
Images are optional and should not be invented unless the request makes imagery relevant.
postconditions: One rendered lane exists for every declared lane in declaration order.
Every item is rendered in the lane selected by laneKey.
Unknown lane values are reported by validation rather than silently dropped.

components.title: List and card collection
components.summary: Rows, grouped rows, or a responsive card catalog without workflow-lane semantics.

manifest.projection: Rows default to id/title/subtitle/icon and may render imageKey as a thumbnail or imageShape=avatar. When avatar imagery is absent, initialsKey renders a bounded textual avatar. Cards additionally render previewKey, imageKey with imageAltKey, badgeKey and inputs.meta. Configure these input keys when source fields use different names; arbitrary source fields are not visible unless projected or consumed by an action.
manifest.meta_shape: inputs.meta entries require key and may declare label, kind=text|badge|boolean|icon, overflow=wrap|truncate and align=start|center|end. Icon metadata may bind titleKey and colorKey for accessible text and semantic Ionic color. inputs.accentKey may bind a semantic Ionic color to a compact row/card border; arbitrary CSS values are rejected by the Client.
manifest.button_shape: inputs.buttons entries require id and may declare label, itemLabelKey, icon, whenKey and whenEquals. Every such button is repeated for each visible row or card. inputs.headerActions holds compact collection commands beside the heading; an entry may have items:[{id,label,icon}] for a dropdown menu. Opening the parent menu does not dispatch an action; choosing a leaf dispatches click:<leaf-id>. Legacy primaryAction/secondaryAction inputs normalize into headerActions. Bind commands with top-level widget.actions on=click:<buttonId>. itemLabelKey reads a per-record label and falls back to label.
manifest.query_binding: inputs.search is boolean, never an object. To share a ui.queryToolbar value with this static collection, use inputs.filters entries shaped {key,stateKey,operator}; stateKey is the bare page-state key without a $state. prefix. Use operator=contains for text search and equals for exact filters. For equals, each non-All select option value must equal the corresponding record field value; keep user-facing meaning in the option label. Filter definitions do not contain options or equalsField; options belong to ui.queryToolbar controls.
manifest.row_state: For flat list rows, inputs.disabledKey names a boolean field that disables activation; inputs.currentKey names a separate boolean field that bolds the title and marks aria-current=step. Current work is independent of selected detail. Selection and row-button events expose row fields directly as $event.<field>, not $event.item.<field>. updateState params accept direct references or structured expressions such as {kind:'expression',op:'equals',args:['$event.status','ready']}; binary expressions use args and never left/right. A string such as $event.status === 'ready' is not evaluated. Prefer exposing the required boolean on the row and binding $event.<booleanField>.
manifest.static_data: For synthetic rows use widget.dataSource={kind:'static',value:[...]}. The renderer does not read inputs.rows or inputs.items.
manifest.value_labels: meta entries support valueLabels as authored choice fallbacks, or optionsDataSource.kind=resourceQuery with optionValuePath and optionLabelPaths for live related-record captions. Unknown identities remain visible as canonical values; display never changes stored IDs.
manifest.reorder_contract: inputs.reorder={enabled:true,orderKey:<numeric rank field>,axis:'vertical'} enables persisted ordering only for one flat, unfiltered, unpaginated list. Bind on=move to a resourceOperation update with record_id=$event.id and payload=$event.patch. The event also exposes source_id, target_id, previous_id, from_index, to_index, placement, input and a stable move_before/move_after operation. The Client supplies pointer/touch drag, move-up/down buttons and Alt+Arrow keyboard movement; it optimistically updates and rolls back when persistence rejects the move.

responsive.compact: rows or narrower card tracks

limitations: Separate list widgets do not form a semantic Kanban board.
Reordering is disabled while list search, filters, grouping or pagination make the visible order incomplete.
postconditions: Every visible collection item has a stable focus identity.
inputs.pagination=true enables bounded local paging after declared search, filters and sorting; pageSize and pageSizeOptions control the visible slice.
A reorderable list exposes drag and single-step alternatives, announces the resulting position, persists one rank update and rolls the optimistic projection back on rejection.

components.title: Dense table
components.summary: A dense comparison of typed textual, status, boolean, icon, and action columns.

manifest.column_display: columns[*].overflow=wrap|truncate and align=start|center|end are retained at widget ingress. Date, datetime and number cells stay unbroken unless overflow is explicit. Columns support valueI18nPrefix with valueLabels fallback, or optionsDataSource.kind=resourceQuery with optionValuePath and optionLabelPaths for live related-record captions; canonical stored IDs are unchanged.

responsive.compact: bounded horizontal overflow by default; inputs.compactPresentation=cards renders each row as a labeled comparison card

postconditions: Declared columns map to rendered cells in declaration order.
inputs.headerActions renders compact collection commands beside the heading; inputs.buttons renders explicit per-record commands in the trailing actions column.

inputs.selectedStateKey plus selectionIndicator=radio exposes the selected record visually and with aria-selected. The radio marker selects without dispatching collectionRowActivated; activating the rest of the row may independently reveal a details widget whose inputs.activationSourceWidgetId matches this table id. relationshipEmphasis={stateKey,fieldKey} keeps the full collection visible while softly marking related rows.
inputs.compactPresentation=cards preserves the same columns and row actions while replacing compact horizontal overflow with labeled row cards; desktop remains tabular.

columns[*].sortable=true enables local sorting before pagination; inputs.sort={key,direction} selects the initial order. Sorting is unavailable for server-paginated data. kind=datetime formats an ISO timestamp in the active locale and local timezone.

Page size and declared filter modes persist within the active subnet, page scope and widget identity. inputs.preferences=false disables persistence; inputs.preferences.filterStateKeys adds explicit scalar filter modes. Search, selection, records and cursors are not persisted. inputs.refresh=true adds a targeted datasource reload button.

components.title: Typed form
components.summary: Typed data capture with validation and bounded form lifecycle actions.

manifest.layout_property: inputs.layout is an optional string enum: stack, responsiveGrid, responsive-grid, grid, or auto-grid. It is not a page layout object.
manifest.static_content: staticContent renders content or markdown as guidance. A content string equal to $state.<path> reads the current page-state value at that path; missing values render empty, not the expression. Other content strings render literally; arbitrary template interpolation is not supported. Its technical field id is never a visible heading; declare label or title only when a user-facing heading is useful.
manifest.enabled_state: Fields default to editable. Literal disabled=true, readonly=true or readOnly=true disables a field; these field properties are booleans, not expressions. Controls are also disabled while uploading/submitting, while a selected record is loading, when inputs.readOnlyIf matches that stored record, or while declared choice options are unavailable. Do not remove these guards or fabricate permission/consent to enable a control. Expose a concrete loading/unavailable/read-only reason and fix the underlying datasource or authorization. visibleIf controls visibility, not authorization.
manifest.conditional_required: Set required=true on the dependent field and use a string visibleIf expression such as $state.result === 'defect'. ui.form evaluates the expression against a snapshot that includes sibling form values and validates visible required fields before submit. Never use an object-shaped condition or synthesize errors with updateState.
manifest.record_editor: A resourceQuery with query.id=$state.<selection> loads the selected record into local fields. Empty selection means create mode, not the first returned record. inputs.buttons[*].id dispatches only matching actions[*].id in declaration order. Post-success steps share that SAME id; on=submit alone does not bind them. False/throw (including cancelled confirmation) stops the sequence. Multiple unrelated submit mutations must never execute together. Declared button enabledIf controls availability. closeOnSuccess dismisses the editor only after a successful command.
manifest.dynamic_record_editor: For trusted provider-projected schemas, inputs.recordsPath selects a record collection from the authenticated dataSource result; fieldsPath selects formField declarations in the chosen record and valuesPath selects their values. selectedStateKey chooses the record. Provider data cannot supply actions, option sources, or upload/read targets; declared package actions use $event.record for immutable identity and expected revision and $event.values for the typed draft. Missing or malformed dynamic fields block submission.
manifest.state_initialized_creation: A form without dataSource hydrates fields from page state using each field's stateKey (alias state_key), defaulting to form.<widget.id>.<field.id>. Before opening a creation modal, updateState initializes draft-specific keys, including a selected parent, and clears old values. defaultValue/default/value are literals, not $state expressions. A dataSource form instead loads the selected record; it does not hydrate page-state fields, and an empty selected id ignores returned records. Use a separate state-initialized create form when parent defaults are needed. Show the parent caption through live choices or an explicitly bound read-only caption.
manifest.state_commit: A stateKey hydrates a local field but does not commit changes by default. inputs.autoCommit=true (alias commitOnChange=true) writes each editable change to that field's stateKey immediately, with number/integer values converted to numbers. Use this opt-in for local sidebar controls such as imageCompare.brushRadiusStateKey; a buttonless form otherwise leaves the editor radius unchanged. This updates only PageState and does not save records or call tools. Keep autoCommit off on forms whose draft must be submitted atomically through $event.values.
manifest.draft_snapshot: A selected-record form can opt into inputs.draftStateKey plus an explicit inputs.draftFields string array. It publishes a detached adaos.ui.form_draft.v1 PageState snapshot {scopeId,sourceId,revision,generation,version,ready,dirty,values}; only declared visible answer fields in draftFields are exported. Initial values, unsaved edits and restored record drafts are included without saving or submitting. ready means the selected record and fields are available, not validation or authorization. External commands must require ready and matching sourceId, retain their existing guards, and use owning tool validation. Values clear and ready=false during selection/loading gaps and disposal; superseded instances and late responses from another scope cannot overwrite a current publisher. Example: a toolbar calls mask analysis with goal=$state.retouch_goal_draft.values.target_area while the right-hand form declares draftStateKey=retouch_goal_draft and draftFields=[target_area].
manifest.modal_composition: ui.application.modals is an object keyed by the literal modal id, never an array. Each modal value is a wrapper {title, presentation:{kind:'modal'}, schema:{id, layout, widgets:[...]}}. The nested schema is a complete page schema: its layout includes version:2 plus pattern, density, contentWidth, scroll, regions and interaction. Put ui.form and any companion command widgets inside modal.schema.widgets; a widget is not itself a modal definition. Open a local declared modal with {type:'navigateModal',params:{modalId:'<literal-id>'}}; target is not the modal id. Use navigate with params.to only for a declared public view.
manifest.read_only_record: inputs.readOnlyIf is evaluated against the stored selected record, not the draft or page state. The Prototype resource provider enforces the same declared read_only_when predicate before update/delete.
manifest.live_choices: A choice field may use optionsDataSource.kind=resourceQuery, optionValuePath and optionLabelPaths. Automation also admits kind=skill with name, params and invalidationTags, or kind=mcp with an admitted public Root MCP toolId, arguments, dryRun=true and resultPath; return an array or {items:[...]}. Related record invalidation refreshes options without resetting the draft; unavailable or malformed options block submission and expose retry. Prototype relationships validate current references atomically, including deletion of referenced targets. Collection filter options remain seed-based pending separate live-lookup qualification. Read-only captions in tables, list metadata and details support Resource Workbench sources; absent captions expose the canonical identity.
manifest.free_form_string_lists: tagInput captures an ordered, deduplicated string array from comma or Enter-delimited values. Use it for open vocabularies such as scopes, roles, identifiers, and evidence references; use chips only for a closed predefined option set.
manifest.prototype_attachments: fileUpload with fileStorage=prototype uploads bytes through the authenticated Preview resource endpoint and stores a string reference (or array for multiple=true). Submit waits for upload; failure retains the old value. Limits: 10 MiB/file, 64 MiB/resource.
manifest.production_attachments: fileUpload with fileStorage=skill, qualified uploadTarget/readTarget from the same owned skill, and maxBytes <= 67108864 sends raw bytes through the normal authorized tool ingress. The upload tool consumes the one-use binary context into storage.blob; the read tool authorizes retrieval. The stored value is an authenticated /api/tools/... attachment reference. Without fileStorage, forms collect metadata only.

responsive.compact: one column when fields no longer fit

postconditions: Every required answer is represented by a typed field.

components.title: Selected item details
components.summary: A readable field projection for one selected or bound record.

manifest.presentation: Use inputs.presentation='section' when details are one compact dashboard or page section, 'header' for a primary record header, 'media' for inspectable media, and the default card only for a genuinely framed detail surface.
manifest.static_data: For one synthetic record use widget.dataSource={kind:'static',value:{...}}. With inputs.selectedStateKey, put keyed records directly in value, for example value:{'item-1':{...},'item-2':{...}}; do not wrap them in records or put selectedId in the value. Field path/key/id reads from the selected record; inputs.fields[*].value may be a selected-record {path} template or a direct $state.path reference/display template, but is not itself a data source. The visible widget heading belongs in top-level widget.title, including a dynamic value such as $state.selectedItemTitle; inputs.title is ignored. Remove title_i18n when title is dynamic because localization is applied before state or selected-record interpolation and would replace the dynamic template.
manifest.value_labels: Field entries support valueLabels as authored choice fallbacks, or optionsDataSource.kind=resourceQuery with optionValuePath and optionLabelPaths for live related-record captions. Unknown identities remain visible; labels do not mutate records.
manifest.media: inputs.mediaKey binds an image/video/audio source on the selected record. Optional mediaKindKey selects image, video or audio; mediaPosterKey binds a poster. inputs.imageKey binds a still image; imageShape=avatar presents compact profile imagery, with initialsKey as the bounded fallback when no image exists. Native controls, loading, unavailable and empty states are provided. A filename field without mediaKey or imageKey is not a viewer.
manifest.commands: Actions sharing named on=click:<command> execute in declaration order; awaited false/throw stops the sequence. Every visible item.details command requires label on one action step. Generic on=click actions remain independent. enabledIf guards the command; repeated clicks are blocked while it is pending. For keyed static details, command params should use $state.selectedId (or another page-state key); there is no implicit $record command context.

responsive.compact: detail surface

postconditions: When selectedStateKey is used, visible details change with that selected key.

components.title: Hierarchy tree
components.summary: Hierarchical navigation for files, lifecycle nodes, and nested domain records.

responsive.compact: nested outline

postconditions: Every selectable leaf provides all fields consumed by its select action.

components.title: Command surface
components.summary: Explicit toolbar, segmented, stack, compact, or automatically overflowing commands.

manifest.button_priority: number; higher values remain visible longer
manifest.appearance: appearance=quiet removes the enclosing toolbar fill while retaining command boundaries and focus feedback.
manifest.section_header: variant=header with appearance=quiet and icon-bearing buttons renders widget.title as a section heading and those icon commands at its trailing edge. Use it for infrequent contextual actions such as unlink/delete: declare a recognizable icon, a complete label for tooltip and aria-label, kind=danger, an explicit confirmation contract, and visibleIf/enabledIf guards. Do not use it as a primary command bar.
manifest.activity_status: statusActivityPath and statusActivityValues may mark a status projection as actively generating or validating; this is presentation only and does not establish completion.
manifest.scope: commands only; use a details or list component for passive status text. A standalone ui.actions widget has page state and click-event context, not an implicit selected $record; selection-dependent commands must use explicit $state keys populated by the selecting collection.

interactions.menu: adaptiveToolbar buttons with options use a viewport-bounded overlay. Selection emits select:<buttonId> with the option as $event (id/value/menu_id), not $event.option. displaySelectedLabel=false keeps a short authored trigger label; optionMetaPaths chooses localized secondary option fields. An option with current=true marks the actual current step in bold and with aria-current, independently of the selected item being inspected. disabled=true prevents selecting an unavailable option. Selection does not execute another command implicitly.
interactions.overflow: variant=autoOverflow keeps required and higher-priority plain commands visible, moves remaining commands into one keyboard-accessible More menu, and recomputes on container resize. Mark a command overflow=never when it owns a nested option menu or must remain visible.

responsive.compact: wraps or uses one explicit overflow menu without overlapping

postconditions: Every declared button has an executable or explicitly disabled action contract.

A static menu may opt into rememberSelection=true with a top-level selectedStateKey for presentation preferences. The browser remembers only a declared scalar option, isolated by subnet/page/widget/button. Restoring never dispatches actions; unknown saved values are ignored. Do not persist workflow authority, entity selection, drafts or secrets this way.

components.title: Collection search and filters
components.summary: Compact page-scoped query controls with filter disclosure, active values and atomic reset.

manifest.control_shape: inputs.controls contains 1..12 entries shaped exactly {id,label,label_i18n?,kind:'search'|'filter',stateKey,inputType:'search'|'text'|'date'|'number'|'select',options?}. stateKey is a bare page-state identifier such as appSearch, never $state.appSearch. select controls require options [{value,label,label_i18n?}]. Controls do not accept placeholder, placeholder_i18n, resetLabel or resetLabel_i18n; the renderer owns compact disclosure, active values and reset UI.
manifest.collection_binding: Bind the same bare stateKey in collection filters. For ui.list use inputs.filters [{key,stateKey,operator:'contains'|'equals'|...}]. Query-toolbar options stay on the control and are not copied into list filters.
manifest.initial_state: For an initial collection read, initialize search/filter keys in pageSchema.initialState or the local modal schema.initialState, e.g. {appSearch:''}. QueryToolbar displays an absent value as empty but does not write that value on mount. An unresolved $state reference in skill/API dataSource params suppresses dispatch; an optional backend argument default does not initialize Client page state. Do not leave an initial gallery read waiting for the first keystroke.

responsive.desktop: search and commands in one row, expandable filter grid
responsive.compact: wraps within available width

interactions.state: Each inputs.controls entry binds one stateKey in the current page scope. Bind the collection resourceQuery to the same $state key. Date commits on native change; numbers and boolean options retain their types.

postconditions: Reset clears all owned query keys in one update without clearing unrelated page state.

components.title: Boolean toggle
components.summary: One explicit binary setting with a boolean change event.

responsive.compact: one full-width setting row

interactions.event: The change event is {value:boolean, checked:boolean}; bind page state with $event.checked.

postconditions: The visible checked state and emitted value are boolean.

components.title: Option selector
components.summary: One compact selectable option set with optional search.

responsive.compact: viewport-bounded popup

postconditions: The selected value maps to one declared option value.

components.title: Section tabs
components.summary: A semantic tab list for switching peer sections within one surface.

manifest.selection: Set inputs.selectedStateKey to the page-state key that stores the active button id. Button ids must equal the values written to that state key. Prefer one on=click updateState action with <selectedStateKey>=$event.id. Do not put selectedStateKey on individual tab buttons and do not prefix the key with $state.
manifest.dynamic_collection: To bind an authenticated collection, declare widget.dataSource plus inputs.itemsPath (defaults to items), itemIdPath, itemLabelPath and optional itemActivityPath/itemIconPath/itemDisabledPath. The renderer maps only inert presentation fields and preserves the source item as $event.record. Provider data cannot define actions, enabledIf, visibleIf or option sources. Set dataSource.preserveLastValue=true when last-known tabs should remain visible during refresh or transport degradation.
manifest.fixed_commands: Compose package-owned commands such as Add with inputs.fixedButtons and optional fixedPlacement=start|end. A fixed id wins over a colliding projected id. Keep its action in the widget actions list; never obtain actions from collection data.
manifest.dynamic_event: An on=click:dynamic action runs only for projected collection items and receives {id,label,activity?,icon?,disabled?,record,ts}. Use $event.id for selectedStateKey and $event.record only for immutable projected identity or display metadata. Fixed commands keep their own click:<fixedButtonId> actions and do not trigger click:dynamic.
manifest.loading_unavailable: The widget host exposes loading, refreshing, stale, unavailable and error states with retry. With preserveLastValue the previous collection remains rendered and is marked stale; without a previous value only fixedButtons remain. A data source in a user-opened modal or comparable foreground surface may declare readPriority=interactive so it runs before queued background reads; this changes queue order only and never bypasses admission or adds concurrency.
manifest.overflow: Use inputs.variant='tabsWithMore' when the tab set is dynamic, can grow, or must stay bounded on compact widths. The client renders visible tabs and moves the remainder into an accessible More menu instead of resetting horizontal scroll. inputs.itemsLimit may impose an optional upper visible-item bound.
manifest.activity: A button with state or activity equal to online or updating receives a Taiga Pulse marker (green for online, warning for updating). Keep the state in visible label or accessible text too: motion and color are supplementary, and reduced-motion users retain the static marker.
manifest.open_and_load_order: When one click opens a surface and also performs a fallible callSkill refresh, dispatch reset/updateState first, navigate second, and the fallible refresh last. Command chains stop after a failed action, so putting refresh before navigate can strand the user without the requested surface. Prefer an on-mount refresh inside the opened surface when available.

responsive.compact: TabsWithMore overflow menu when inputs.variant is tabsWithMore

postconditions: The active tab is exposed through aria-selected.
ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home, and End move keyboard focus between enabled tabs.

components.title: Breadcrumb navigation
components.summary: A compact hierarchy path with an explicit current location.

responsive.compact: horizontally scrollable path without label overlap

postconditions: The last or explicitly current item uses aria-current=page.
Navigation labels may truncate visually but retain their full accessible name.

components.title: Accordion disclosure
components.summary: A bounded list of independently disclosed information sections.

bindings.lazyDataSources: Package-owned map from item id to a standard read dataSource. The renderer starts it only while that item is expanded and never executes sources returned by runtime data.

responsive.compact: full-width disclosure list

postconditions: Each trigger exposes aria-expanded and owns one labelled region.
Single-open is the default; multiple=true explicitly enables multiple open sections.
A lazy item exposes loading and unavailable states and can preserve the last successful value through its standard dataSource policy.

components.title: Governed public-site preview
components.summary: An inspectable same-origin preview of a retained public-site projection.

manifest.semantic_surface: Use capability_surfaces with capability_ref=visual.sitePreview. Declare site_id and a relative route; the semantic compiler owns the runtime widget mapping.

inputs.minHeight: bounded preview height from 320 to 1200 pixels

manifest.security: The Client derives /site-development/<siteId>/ and rejects arbitrary origins, URLs, HTML, CSS and script input.
manifest.draft_preview: An optional widget.dataSource loads adaos.site_preview.v1 {source,projection,route,page}. The isolated static shell verifies site/route identity and the complete canonical SHA256 digest chain before atomic apply and acknowledges that exact digest. Use explicit read policy and mutation invalidation tags. Tagged saves show progress until render acknowledgement; failed reads, writes, validation or timeout retain the prior preview. Uploaded images must be owned validated inert image bytes or admitted public assets, never credential-bearing URLs.

responsive.desktop: desktop, tablet and mobile viewport inspection inside the main work region
responsive.compact: mobile-width preview with the same governed route

postconditions: Preview identity is a site id plus relative route, never an authored iframe URL.
Viewport controls change only the inspection frame and do not mutate site content.
The rendered site remains isolated in a sandboxed frame.

components.title: Project and chat navigation
components.summary: Native project/chat navigation for an owner-admitted project-conversation service; bounded chat search, archive and CRUD.

manifest.connection: Declare service/session and protocol=adaos.project-conversation.v2. Share the identical connection with ui.projectConversation and item.conversationContext. Selection/drafts are local projections; server validates project/chat ownership. Do not invent this protocol for a skill that does not implement it.

responsive.compact: Keyboard-accessible drawer

postconditions: Chat refs include the parent project; duplicate names do not determine identity.
Declarative service names grant no authority.

components.title: Project conversation
components.summary: Native bounded chat with isolated drafts, per-chat model/reasoning/tools and shared Markdown/math/copy presentation.

manifest.connection: Owner implements adaos.project-conversation.v2. Declare content:{format:markdown,copy:true,plainCopy:true}; optional icon is an admitted resource reference. Profiles use revision CAS, provider capabilities and immutable run snapshots. No credentials, app-specific URLs, bots or universal effort enum in the page.

responsive.desktop: Dedicated main region with bounded scroll history
responsive.compact: Wrapping controls and pinned composer

postconditions: Late results and uploads retain the originating chat.
Copy preserves original Markdown and reports clipboard denial.
Read/share/automatic outputs require separately admitted owner operations.

components.title: Chat context inspector
components.summary: Project library, explicit chat source membership, revisioned memory/context, extraction versions and opt-in original-document retention.

manifest.connection: Share the native project-conversation connection. The owner stores and validates source/version membership and budgets. Project-shared memory requires explicit consent; chat-derived memory remains isolated. Uploaded text alone is neither RAG nor original-file archival.

responsive.compact: Focus-trapped context panel

postconditions: Selected sources and memory revisions are inspectable.
A source deletion revokes readable versions/originals; history retention is explicit.

components.title: Conversation surface
components.summary: Reusable owner-scoped conversation UX: text/voice composer, declared attachments and model control, fixed/selectable agent, independent history filter, bounded scroll pagination and factual run status.

conversation_contract.agent: fixed requires id/label; select requires a registry source. Current recipient and history.allAgents are independent. A fixed owner never follows the global dialog selector.
conversation_contract.history: mode=auto loads one bounded older cursor page on upward scroll; maxMessages bounds retained client history. Platform streams use conversation.history.more; application feeds declare on=history.more using $event.cursor and return messages/has_more_before/before_cursor through the same source with owner invalidation. Without either provider there is no fabricated pager. allAgents is opt-in for an authorized aggregate feed, not a broadcast recipient.
conversation_contract.attachments: Omit unless the owner supports uploaded references through a declared on=send action; the legacy voice.chat.user transport is not an attachment ingestion API. Declare uploadTarget/readTarget, accept, maxFiles/maxBytes. on=send receives attachments:[{ref,name,mime,size_bytes}], text, meta and retry-stable request_id. Never embed bytes in message context.
conversation_contract.model: Canonical source/valuePath/optionsPath; profilePath and revisionPath together enable the shared model/reasoning picker. Models advertise capabilities:{efforts,default,web_search,source}, capability_revision and availability. on=model.change receives value, profile, expected_revision, capability_revision for an owner CAS mutation. Unknown reasoning metadata permits provider default only. Runs retain admitted profiles.
conversation_contract.content: presentation.content:{format:markdown,copy:true,plainCopy:true} enables shared sanitized Markdown/math and exact-message Copy. Original Markdown stays canonical. Raw HTML and remote images never execute/fetch on render. Copy denial has actionable feedback; optional plain copy uses derived rendered text.
conversation_contract.voice: Opt-in shared microphone control; Voice application is not a dependency.
conversation_contract.run: Source may publish run:{id,status,label?}; accepted/queued/started/running/progress/input_required/resumed/completed/failed/cancelled/unknown are factual events. No fabricated timed stage labels.
conversation_contract.presentation: floating opts into the Client shell's single persistent drag/resize/minimize session. Window geometry and minimized-button position are independent. The resolved owner, routing scope, current addressee and visible bounded tail are snapshotted at detach; unrelated scenario state does not transfer authority. It is not a browser popup or a permission grant.

inputs.fillHeight: true for a first-class full-height conversation destination
inputs.multiline: true for a growing multiline composer
inputs.sendCommand: voice.chat.user for the platform conversation channel; omit for an application-owned declarative send action
inputs.meta: optional conversation_id, conversation_topic_id, dialog_channel_id and thread_id routing metadata

manifest.declarative_send: Bind widget.actions on=send to normal callSkill/updateState actions for an application-owned chat. The event includes text, meta and retry-stable request_id. The composer awaits successful completion, disables duplicate sends, and retains a failed draft. Read {messages:[{id,from,text,ts,actions?}]} through a skill dataSource with explicit cache/invalidation policy. The application enforces authority, persists discussion and validates all LLM proposals; the renderer does not route this through the platform NLU.

live_data_source.params: optional routing state references matching inputs.meta

manifest.prototype_data_source: Use kind=static with a bounded message array when a live conversation is explicitly out of scope. Omit sendCommand when the composer must be read-only.

data_shape.record: {id,from,text,ts}; assistant messages may include agent metadata and actions

events: send via declared sendCommand or on=send
history.more via declared bounded owner action

responsive.desktop: fills its dedicated region when fillHeight=true
responsive.compact: one bounded conversation column with history and composer

postconditions: A first-class conversation destination declares layout.scroll=regions and one main region containing only ui.chat with fillHeight=true. Optional toolbar and navigation regions stay visible at all widths; only the message feed scrolls. Application, variant and region IDs do not select this capability.
A visible composer has an explicit sendCommand or widget.actions on=send; a static read-only transcript has no decorative composer.
Conversation routing metadata is explicit when the stream is scoped to a channel or thread.

components.title: Installed application launcher
components.summary: The canonical subnet desktop projection for pinned application launchers and application catalog collections.

manifest.desktop_projection: For the authoritative pinned desktop launcher use the stable widget id 'desktop-icons', type 'collection.grid', and widget.dataSource={kind:'y',transform:'desktop.icons'}. The stable id activates platform layout customization, drag/reorder and responsive desktop behavior. This projection owns installed and pinned application identity, ordering and launch metadata; do not replace it with a skill list or static records.
manifest.selection: Use on=select with the projection's $event.action.navigate and $event.launchModal. The tile itself is the primary action; do not add a redundant Open button.
manifest.catalog_projection: Catalog collections may use kind='y' with an explicit catalog path, but installation lifecycle belongs to the Applications scenario.

data_shape.record: Platform-owned launcher item including stable id, icon, title, action and optional launchModal/channel badge

responsive.desktop: responsive application tile grid with platform-owned ordering
responsive.compact: bounded launcher grid without per-tile command clutter

postconditions: The desktop launcher reads the desktop.icons Yjs projection rather than authored or static application records.
The desktop.icons launcher uses stable widget id desktop-icons so platform layout controls remain active.
Selecting a tile follows platform launch metadata and does not simulate installation lifecycle.

components.title: Installed desktop widgets
components.summary: The canonical system projection for widgets installed and pinned to the current desktop.

manifest.required_data_source: widget.dataSource must equal {kind:'y',transform:'desktop.widgets'}; this component is not a generic authored content container.
manifest.ownership: The platform projection owns installed, pinned, removed and reordered widget state. Keep widget catalog management connected to the established desktop runtime instead of emulating it with local state.

data_shape.record: Platform-owned installed widget contribution and placement

responsive.desktop: responsive installed-widget regions controlled by the desktop runtime
responsive.compact: single ordered widget flow with platform controls

postconditions: The component reads the desktop.widgets Yjs projection.
Install, pin, unpin, remove and reorder behavior remains owned by the platform desktop runtime.

components.title: Metric or status tile
components.summary: A compact independent metric, health or status informer for dashboard composition.

manifest.static_data: Use widget.dataSource={kind:'static',value:{value,label,description,color,icon,buttons}} for a prototype tile. Text must communicate state without relying on color. Use color=muted or offline for last-known data from an unavailable source.
manifest.authoritative_projection: When another installed capability already publishes the required state and action eligibility, bind to that Yjs projection and dispatch its existing public action target. Do not duplicate transition rules or invent parallel commands.

inputs.valuePath: optional payload path for the primary status or metric
inputs.labelPath: optional payload path for the short supporting label
inputs.descriptionPath: optional payload path for concise explanatory text
inputs.colorPath: optional payload path for success, warning, danger, or primary tone
inputs.iconPath: optional payload path for an Ionicon name; inputs.icon is the static fallback

manifest.composition: For peer dashboard tiles, declare one layout region with role=status per tile and put one visual.metricTile in each region. role=main spans the dashboard width. Several tiles in one region remain one vertical block. Dynamic payload buttons use click:<actionId>; preserve the source projection's visibility and action IDs.

responsive.desktop: compact peer tile in a responsive dashboard grid
responsive.compact: full-width tile in stable semantic order

postconditions: The primary status is understandable from text and icon without color.
Peer tiles use separate layout regions so wide and compact ordering is deterministic.
Offline or stale last-known values use an explicit text label and muted visual tone; their unavailable actions are omitted or disabled.

components.title: Metric chart
components.summary: A bounded chart projection for metric or timeseries values.

responsive.compact: bounded chart

postconditions: A non-empty numeric series produces a non-blank chart.

components.title: Multi-metric arc
components.summary: A compact concentric arc for two to six independent normalized usage or health metrics.

manifest.static_data: Use dataSource={kind:'static',value:{metrics:[{id,label,value,display,description?}],value?,label?,subtitle?,description?,buttons?}}. Values are independently normalized against inputs.max (100 by default), not parts of one total.

inputs.metricsPath: optional payload path for the metric array; defaults to metrics
inputs.metrics: optional static or prototype fallback metric array used when metricsPath resolves to an empty collection
inputs.centerValuePath: optional payload path for the center value
inputs.centerLabelPath: optional payload path for the center label
inputs.subtitlePath: optional payload path for concise context
inputs.descriptionPath: optional payload path for a short fallback description
inputs.centerValue: optional static or prototype fallback center value
inputs.centerLabel: optional static or prototype fallback center label
inputs.subtitle: optional static or prototype fallback subtitle
inputs.description: optional static or prototype fallback description
inputs.buttons: optional fallback action buttons, dispatched as click:<buttonId>

manifest.composition: Use one multi-metric arc instead of unrelated peer tiles when CPU/RAM/Disk or a few quota dimensions belong to one conceptual group. Do not use it for values with incompatible scales unless they are normalized first.

responsive.desktop: arc and concise legend side by side
responsive.compact: arc above the legend in one card

postconditions: Every ring has a visible text label and value; color is never the only carrier of meaning.
Independent metrics share a declared maximum or are normalized before rendering.
The widget remains one semantic group when the dashboard wraps.

recipes.title: Image annotation workspace
recipes.summary: Compose a resizable image workspace, contextual tools, native result layers and authoritative task progress.

composition.layout: Use workbench, scroll=regions, main plus inspector, and shared toolbar/commands regions. Declare inspector.size={minPx:320,preferredPx:370,maxPx:560,resizable:true,remember:true}. Compact inspector uses sheet or drawer. No application-specific CSS.
composition.main: A sizing=fill layout.group contains a header-slot contextual tool group and a body-slot sizing=fill visual.imageCompare. Use editorStateKey/editorCommandStateKey for external tools, and maskToolbar=false to avoid duplicate controls.
composition.layers: Provider pair.annotations follows image.annotations.v1.schema.json. Separate original and result alpha, focus and protection layers by stable IDs and roles. Keep raster bases native and immutable; ordered add/subtract corrections are draft data. Never reuse another result contour.
composition.drafts: Atomically save form draft, context crop and annotationDraft before submitting one idempotent server command. Clear dirty only after exact draft generation/version acknowledgement; failed persistence blocks submission.
composition.job: Read one authoritative task into feedback.taskProgress. Bind cancel to an owning server command with run_id=$event.run_id and revision=$event.revision. Acknowledgement never fabricates cancellation or completion. Reload only observes.
composition.selection: ui.list cards show result thumbnails and metadata. Selecting a historical result changes viewed artifact only; keep active job, current draft, selected result and explicit final reference separate.

unsupported: The renderer does not implement AI inference, segmentation, compositing, a job scheduler, connector authorization or export ownership. Those remain owning service capabilities.
postconditions: The same schema has consistent desktop and modal geometry.
All processing commands use one owning application and webspace context.
Raw and reviewed artifacts remain accessible independently of job status.
Unknown input fields fail validation before rendering.

recipes.title: Kanban resource board
recipes.summary: Map any typed resource collection into explicit ordered workflow lanes.

inputs.laneKey: Resource field containing a lane id.
inputs.cardFields: Optional typed field projections shown on compact cards.

dataSource.forbidden_kind: local_crud is a provider mode, never a WebUI dataSource.kind

composition.visual_rule: Use compact text-first cards. Add images only when the request explicitly makes imagery relevant.

interactions.drag_drop: Set inputs.dragDrop=true and declare an on=move persistence action. Prefer resourceOperation(update) with record_id=$event.id and payload=$event.patch for ordinary field changes.
interactions.crud: Compose resourceQuery, resourceOperation, ui.form, and item.details before adding skill-specific handlers.

postconditions: The page contains one collection.board widget.
The declared lane count equals the requested column count.
Every requested sample card belongs to exactly one declared lane.
Every lane contains the requested number of sample cards when specified.

recipes.title: Resource board workbench
recipes.summary: Compose query controls, a board projection, record details, and typed CRUD over one Resource Workbench definition.

composition.query: Toolbar controls write typed search/filter/sort values to page state; resourceQuery consumes those values.
composition.board: collection.board projects query items by laneKey and writes selection to state.
composition.details: item.details or a modal reads the selected resource record; ui.form edits it.
composition.operations: resourceOperation implements create/update/delete and lane-field updates; domain commands remain separate.

prototype.provider_mode: The separate PrototypeData artifact uses mode=local_crud; never put local_crud in WebUI dataSource.kind.
prototype.records: Return prototype_records beside webui in adaos.builder.webui_result.v1 so Builder can materialize the disposable provider.
prototype.forms: Use ui.form inputs.fields with formInputType values. For a choice field use select, dropdown, or combobox; selector is invalid and input.selector is a separate standalone widget.

board_create_entry.rule: The create-item modal contains a ui.form with title and laneKey fields; do not add a repeated per-card Add button.

prototype.modal_rule: When navigateModal is used, declare that exact literal id under ui.application.modals and provide a schema object containing widgets. In a complete JSON document use create-item, never @create-item; @<id> is reserved for JSON Patch pointer paths.

postconditions: Changing a query control changes the resource query rather than filtering an unrelated client copy.
Selecting a card identifies one stable resource record for details or editing.
Ordinary CRUD does not require a generated skill-specific handler.
Every mutation is checked against the ResourceDefinition operation and role policy.

recipes.title: Resource collection workbench
recipes.summary: Compose a list or table, record details, and typed local CRUD over one generic Prototype resource.

composition.scope: This recipe materializes exactly one Prototype resource. Use static bounded reference choices unless another admitted recipe explicitly declares multiple resources.
composition.collection: Use ui.list or ui.table with widget.dataSource.kind=resourceQuery and one prototype.<resource_name> resourceType. dataSource is a widget peer of inputs, never inputs.dataSource.
composition.selection: Write the selected stable record id to page state and use the same id for details and updates.
composition.operations: Put resourceOperation declarations in widget.actions for create, update, and delete. updateState alone is not persistence.

prototype.records: Return prototype_records beside WebUI so Builder can derive and materialize the disposable local CRUD provider.

postconditions: Mutations target the same prototype resourceType used by the collection query.
Every requested mutation has a resourceOperation instead of a decorative state-only action.
Ordinary local CRUD does not require a generated skill-specific handler.

recipes.title: Master and detail
recipes.summary: Select one collection item and show a state-bound detail surface.

composition.selection: Master writes selected id; details read the same id.

postconditions: Selecting different master records changes the visible detail record.

recipes.title: Typed data entry
recipes.summary: Capture a typed record and expose explicit lifecycle actions.
postconditions: Each requested answer has one editable typed field.

recipes.title: Copyable identifier
recipes.summary: Turn a visible identifier into an explicit clipboard action with immediate success or failure feedback.

composition.projection: Use item.details and set copyable=true on the identifier field. Keep the full identifier visible or available through an accessible name. The Taiga copy affordance is local UI behavior and never requires a skill, permission, or approval.
composition.fallback_action: copyToClipboard remains a supported compatibility fallback when the value is outside item.details, but new detail projections should prefer a copyable field.
composition.feedback: The standard copy component supplies immediate localized copied/failed feedback; do not add a second copy button.

postconditions: Activating the identifier or its copy affordance writes the intended full value to the clipboard.
Success and failure both produce explicit transient feedback.
Copying an identifier is handled locally without a governed runtime command.

recipes.title: Canonical choice values and executable filters
recipes.summary: Keep agent schemas, persisted enum tokens, UI option values, filter parameters, and localized display labels aligned end to end.

domain.rule: Declare one canonical token set and reuse it unchanged in the agent/content JSON Schema enum, persisted record, skill handler validation, query parameter, and every UI option.value. User-facing labels are presentation only.

query.rule: Use ui.queryToolbar controls to write page state immediately. Bind a skill dataSource param or ui.list filter to the same bare state key. A ui.form field merely hydrated with stateKey is not an executable live filter.

composition.display: For ui.list metadata and item.details fields, map canonical tokens with valueLabels or valueI18nPrefix/optionsDataSource. Never persist or filter on a translated label, and never expose a raw token such as over_60 when a label map is declared.
composition.agent_boundary: Validate the completed agent payload against the same closed enum before persistence. Do not repair an unknown token by guessing; return invalid_output with bounded diagnostics. Normalize presentation-only text separately from canonical identifiers.
composition.generated_multiline_text: For generated fields rendered as Markdown, declare contentMediaType: text/markdown on that string in the content JSON Schema. Content Generation then normalizes literal \n and \r\n sequences at the provider boundary before validation and persistence. Do not decode escapes globally or apply this annotation to identifiers, paths, code, or canonical enum values.

unsupported: A buttonless ui.form is not a live query toolbar.
Translated labels are not storage or filter identities.
Agent prompts alone do not enforce enum compatibility; the structured schema and application validation must do so.
postconditions: Changing a query control causes the bound dataSource to re-execute with the selected canonical value.
Every stored choice token belongs to the declared closed enum.
Every visible canonical token has a localized or authored label without changing its stored value.
The agent output schema, handler constants, UI option values, and filter parameters contain the same token set.
Generated Markdown fields contain real line breaks after admission, while undeclared strings remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

recipes.title: Durable media-backed records
recipes.summary: Publish image, audio, or video bytes through the AdaOS media store, persist a browser-safe descriptor, and bind it to supported Client inputs.

producer.generated_image: Use adaos.sdk.llm.images.generate/get with one stable request_id. A completed response already contains a published browser media descriptor in response.media; generation_pending must poll the same request instead of submitting paid work again.
producer.application_file: For application-owned image, audio, or video bytes use adaos.sdk.io.media.publish_media_file, then adaos.sdk.io.media.browser_media_descriptor. Use publish_media_package for bounded segmented media and register_media_file only for an intentionally retained original under an admitted stable root.
producer.forbidden: Never invent /media paths, persist provider URLs, embed base64 in business records, or expose node-local source/path values to WebUI.

record.rule: Persist the complete browser-safe descriptor object atomically with the owning record only after publication succeeds. Preserve route, path, filename, mime, content_ref, and size_bytes plus verified type-specific metadata returned by the SDK.

renderer.collection_still: For ui.list set the top-level inputs.imageKey to the record field containing the image descriptor. Do not use imagePath or inputs.card.imagePath.
renderer.detail_still: For item.details set the top-level inputs.imageKey to the descriptor field. Do not use imagePath or inputs.media.imagePath.
renderer.detail_mixed_media: For item.details set inputs.mediaKey to the descriptor field. Optionally set mediaKindKey to a record field containing image, audio, or video and mediaPosterKey to an image descriptor used as the poster.

composition.refresh: The read dataSource and the successful mutation action must share the same invalidation tag so the initiating Client refetches the record. Backend-originated changes require an explicit subscribed data route; direct database edits are not UI events.
composition.trial: Trial application data remains isolated, while SDK publication writes content-addressed bytes to the node-authoritative media store used by /media routes. Do not copy files into a trial-local mediaserver directory.

unsupported: A filename or local filesystem path is not a renderable media value.
Nested imagePath aliases are not part of the Client ABI.
Action invalidation is not a backend push subscription.
postconditions: Every persisted media descriptor resolves through its declared browser route after restart and publication.
Collection thumbnails use inputs.imageKey and detail playback uses imageKey or mediaKey at the top level.
A successful media mutation invalidates the same tag declared by its read dataSource.
No provider credential, base64 payload, or node-local path is stored in the application record.

recipes.title: Operational dashboard
recipes.summary: Compose independent metrics and summaries in a responsive area grid.

composition.layout: Independent peer areas using pattern=dashboard or grid.

postconditions: Metric areas use a grid render plan on a sufficiently wide viewport.
